text: The Great Kaan causes bark of trees made into something like paper to pass for money; the narrative explains the imperial currency.
Dr. Bretschneider makes the following remark: Marco Polo seems to be mistaken; paper in China is not made from mulberry-trees but from Broussonetia papyrifera. H. C.

Regarding Bretschneider's statement, p. 430, Dr. B. Laufer writes to me: this is a singular error of Bretschneider; Marco Polo is perfectly correct, and mulberry bark was preferred for making paper-money.
